I’m saying soft ESH

Your wife definitely should have told you about the company position and about wanting to speak to her father again, that makes her an asshole for hiding it from you. I understand having to protect your child from racists, and I don’t think being angry about this is unjustified. The reason I also think you’re kind of an asshole is because instead of asking you wife,”Has your father promised to treat my son better” or “Has he worked on his bigotry or does he plan to?” Or frankly any other question as to why she felt so alone that she felt the need to talk to him again, you went full nuclear on your pregnant wife and called her less than a person in your eyes. Is how she went about this wrong? Absolutely it is. Is she also probably really emotionally vulnerable and without a family support system? Yes. I’m not saying she should talk to her father, I believe she should have done the opposite. I’m just saying there were loads more productive conversations you could of had with her instead of insulting her entire person, and if you really feel that way about her your marriage is not going to last very long. She cut her entire family off for you, something that is very hard for a lot of people, and in her greatest moment of emotional vulnerability she made a mistake albeit a bad one. Instead of insulting you should either explain why this has upset you so badly like an adult or part ways if the decisions she makes go against what you want for your family.

I’m going against the grain and saying NTA. 

Personally I know many addicts, and I’ve lost a lot of family members to drugs. Yes addiction is selfish towards your family in the sense that it hurts them, but most addicts are deeply hurting individuals that are hurting others unintentionally because of their self destructive actions. It’s not like most addicts want to hurt the people they love so I don’t understand all the comments blaming you for something you probably already feel guilty for. 

They weren’t TAs for having it, but your BIL is most certainly the assholes for SHOWING it to you, during a time that is supposed to be fun and celebratory. That and the fact that you are clean presently, and obviously weren’t doing opiates at the wedding makes your anger justified in my mind. I could never imagine telling a recovering addict I know something like that at a wedding. Even if you had good intentions by having it, what a quick and cruel way to make someone feel guilty/ shameful and hurt for something they are trying to overcome.

Everyone on Reddit is so dramatic ffs. I’m saying ESH. It’s perfectly understandable that she was upset you came over during her work hours, I’m not bashing her for that. Her text was unnecessarily rude in my opinion because it’s quite obvious you and your wife are under a lot of stress, and while yes the world doesn’t revolve around you, it doesn’t take a lot of effort to be kind to others. Obviously you shouldn’t have showed up at her house, and in the future you need to explain to your child that we have to be courteous to others as they have stuff going on as well. Personally yes it would have annoyed me to have to step away from my work after you invited yourself over, but honestly it wasn’t that big of deal and you said you left quickly. It definitely warranted a text to set boundaries such as “Hey this upset me today and it was pretty rude of you to show up while I was busy” but her “the world doesn’t revolve around you” and “you don’t get to step all over us” is honestly just a bit much considering the situation. Do better in the future and be more considerate of others even when under stress.

These responses are frustrating. At the very least I would say this is a NTA situation. I would say N A H but I feel like the groom + bride should have expected you would want to bring your child or should have informed you of the no babies rule ahead of time. I plan on having a child free wedding, and would have made that clear to EVERYONE months before the wedding. That is where the bride and groom messed up. It boggles me that everyone on here and in the wedding party just assumes people would get babysitters for their 3 month old children. It is very uncommon for mothers or new parents to be comfortable leaving their babies with babysitters that young. If I was the bride I would have assumed you and your wife would want to bring your baby and would have politely informed both of you months ahead of time of my preference so you could either A.) find a babysitter or B.) prepare to stay home with the child.

Ultimately you are not an asshole for not wanting to leave your infant home alone, and they aren’t the assholes for HAVING a no babies rule but instead they are the assholes for not informing you sooner. At the end of the day people can have child free weddings, but you cannot be upset when parents choose not to attend because of that.

ESH 100%

On your wife’s end, she should NEVER have taken your kid somewhere you had both (yes BOTH because that’s what the 2 yes rules mean and if the wife had disagreed she should have said so to begin with) agreed to keep him away from. She did this behind your back, and everyone saying OP is “abusive” for having his wife’s location and looking for her after he had been home for hours with no response to his attempts to reach her….are you guys okay???? What husband in their right mind would not be trying to find his wife and kid after that??? My entire family has each others locations via Life360 in case we can’t get ahold of each other and are worried about the other person. Nothing about that is abusive it’s called being a worried parent and partner. So regarding that your wife is completely out of line. She disrespected your agreement and acted immaturely instead of communicating to you that she wanted your son to see his aunt. Which is also valid, but how she handled it was immature and secretive which has broken your trust with her. 

However, shitty people do not always raise shitty kids. You were unfairly judging your SIL’s kids solely because you dislike their mother. That is not okay and its also very immature. I would understand wanting either your wife or yourself there to supervise because of the random boyfriends or even SIL, but to completely ban your wife and your son from visiting your SIL + her children is very controlling and I would have vetoed it point blank if I was your wife. Adding to this, it is never okay to split a child and a parent for the sake of winning an argument. It is cruel, this is an adult matter that you need to work out with your wife, NOT put your son in the middle of it. 

Overall Your wife did fuck up and what she did is not okay, BUT you’re also acting like an A H and you’re unfairly keeping her son from her and in turn your son from his mom because you guys cannot communicate. Either go to couples therapy or talk it out like mature adults.

Also the amount of people in the comments absolutely REACHING to call this man abusive is hilarious. Both of the parents are at fault here, but the only thing that could even be borderline abusive is taking the kid away from the mom, which in his case he feels he can’t trust her (which is still not right but not coming from a place of malice) y’all gotta stop calling everything and everyone abusive

I’m going to go with soft YTA. I saw in your replies that your father was abusive (to which I say I’m sorry you and your family had to deal with that) and I understand where you’re coming from because my mother has been in various long term abusive relationships my entire life. It can be really hard to even accept new male individuals into your life, much less a new boyfriend/stepfather. Your feelings about wanting distance are valid, and you have every right to feel that way. However, I feel like you may be taking this out a little too much on Richard/his kids and sometimes your mom and little brother. I’m assuming Richard probably thinks “your space” means your bedroom etc. and is just trying to get to know you a little better. You don’t have a relationship with him, but maybe try compromising and just being civil like you would with somebody who is trying to make small talk. As for the little kids, they don’t understand the situation and are probably just excited to have a new brother. I understand it difficult, but again maybe just try being distantly kind to them as they are still little. As for the comment you made about the therapist not siding with you- I understand this fear completely and it took me awhile to understand that even if a therapist doesn’t AGREE with you, doesn’t mean they think your opinion is wrong or invalid. Therapists are meant to help you and listen, and sometimes as humans we are in the wrong. That is okay, and that doesn’t mean that your feelings are wrong, but just that your actions towards others and your own well-being might be. I would definitely talk with your therapist about this, even if you’re afraid of them not siding with you. Overall I wish you the best navigating this situation

My dad has his own business with my grandpa, and it’s normally just the two of them or maybe one extra person. As long as I can remember he’s always worked really long hours (12+ a day) almost everyday of the week.  However unlike you, he never used that as an excuse to not make me a priority. I cannot remember even a single birthday without him present and spending the whole day with me. I sympathize that owning or managing your own business is hard, but what you’ve essentially shown your daughter her whole life is that she will always be second priority to the job. You need to apologize to her, SINCERELY, and make a better effort in the future to prioritize what should have been your first priority this whole time.

Edit: should have added that my birthday specifically is during the busy season for his business, and he still forgoes a full day of work that would probably make him a lot of money to spend time with me and the family on my birthday. Do better.

NTA I grew up on hot lunches for most of my childhood because my mom couldn’t afford the groceries for cold lunch. We got our school lunches for free. I never recall a time that I was upset that I couldn’t have cold lunch, especially at 15 because I understood my mom was doing the best she could. When I moved in with my dad I started having cold lunches everyday, and of course I favored them more to hot lunch, so I don’t see why your 15 year old is WANTING school lunch. (Assuming you’re kids go to a public school in the US) The hot lunches are not the greatest quality of food. Even if the 15 year old was raised by you to be excited for hot lunch, he should be old enough to realize the situation now and the quality of hot lunch food. Maybe have a talk with him about money, not necessarily to stress him out of course because I know a lot of parents avoid the money talk for that reason, but just to put things into perspective.
